Recent evidence cautions against equating benchmark accuracy with temporal reasoning. Petrov et al. (RecSys 2026) find that recency-weighted pairwise models outperform reproduced SASRec/eSASRec on four of five benchmarks; these models combine independent item-transition signals without contextualizing history items jointly. Include last-item, recency-weighted transition, and popularity baselines under identical evaluation conditions. Results concern specific benchmarks, not these four Amazon categories. [Study](https://www.research.atspotify.com/publications/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-really-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling). Oh and Cho (2024) explicitly measure recency bias; Luo et al. (2024) show learned positional embeddings often capture token distances, motivating separate tests of content and position. [Recency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [position](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793).

History-edit explanations offer useful machinery but establish model sensitivity rather than improved recommendation: Scarcelli et al. (2025) search for minimal discrete history changes that alter recommendations. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606). Practical synthesis—not an established benchmark found in this search: pair fixed-position masking with replacements matched on training frequency and embedding norm; preserve sequence length, padding, final query position, and candidate sets. Compare recent versus old edits, position swaps versus identity replacements, and repeated versus distinct items while controlling recency. Use no-op edits and popularity-matched random histories as negative controls. Synthetic histories with deliberately specified recent/repeated cues provide mechanism checks, not evidence of real-user relevance. Measure paired target-margin/rank changes alongside representation changes to help distinguish encoder sensitivity from scoring effects; positional-embedding ablations can further test positional dependence. Keep diagnostic sensitivity separate from improvement, which requires higher macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator.
